Validated fixes `4.1`, `4.2`, `4.4`, `4.5`, and `4.6` are present in code. I found these remaining issues, including one that overturns the `4.3` “no fix needed” call.

FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.89  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:1591](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1591), findings are called “equivalence classes,” but the implementation uses thresholded similarity plus single-linkage union-find. That relation is not transitive, so `A≈B` and `B≈C` collapse into one class even when `A≈C` is false. I verified this with a custom similarity function: the detector produced one class `['a','b','c']` even though `sim(a,c)=0.1`. This can suppress genuine novelty and inflate convergence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either redefine the model everywhere as graph connectivity instead of equivalence, or switch clustering so every pair inside a class must satisfy `tau_sim` (for example complete-linkage or clique-based clustering).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:1434](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1434) and [dynamic_management.py:1459](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1459), the stopword list removes semantic negators like `not` and `no`. That makes contradictory findings look identical. I verified that `_finding_similarity("null check present", "null check not present") == 1.0`. Convergence can therefore rise when two models actually disagree.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Keep negation-bearing words in the token stream, or add an explicit contradiction penalty before awarding the class-match bonus.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:1772](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1772) and [dynamic_management.py:1844](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1844), the code says “not converged unless `null_expected`,” but no such guard exists. After three empty rounds, the live behavior is `kappa_set=1.0`, `kappa_rate=1.0`, `kappa_adopt=1.0`, and `converged=True`. Silence is treated as perfect convergence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit empty-evidence guard in `converged()` or `kappa()`, requiring at least one cumulative finding class unless `null_expected=True` is passed intentionally.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:2831](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L2831), `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` needs `response_time` and `response_chars` for parser-yield and cost-per-finding checks. But [dynamic_management.py:5157](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5157) calls it with only `(mid, fc, failed)`, so those diagnostics silently receive zeros in real runs. That means the appendix’s `φ_i` / `F_eff` failure mode is detectable in unit tests but effectively dead in the actual manager path.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass `responses[mid].response_time` and `len(responses[mid].content)` through `process_round()`, then run parser-yield remediation before finalising convergence and stop metrics for that round.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: Area 5 says `Y^(<=r) = |F^(<=r)| * H_bar^(<=r)` in [dynamic_management.py:1865](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1865), but [dynamic_management.py:5084](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5084) flattens `FindingEquivalenceClass.members` back into raw findings before computing yield. If three models report the same issue, yield counts three findings, not one deduped class. That inflates `Y`, contaminates `mu`, and can delay stopping on duplicate-heavy rounds.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute `Y` on equivalence classes or a deduped representative set. If multi-model support matters, track support multiplicity separately instead of counting duplicates as new cognitive yield.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The Experiment 15 decision “`4.3` no fix needed” is not mathematically clean. [dynamic_management.py:827](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L827) sets critical-task redundancy to total pool size `K`, but [dynamic_management.py:819](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L819) excludes the PM from standard task execution when `K > 1`. So critical-task target coverage is structurally unreachable before any capacity limit is considered, and [dynamic_management.py:973](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L973) can only warn about a guaranteed degradation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define the target over the admissible execution pool (`K_exec`) or explicitly allow PM participation for critical tasks. The current resolution should not stand as “no fix needed.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py:1991](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1991), the “per-area” vocabulary fix uses `flaw_class` as `area_key`. For decomposed mathmodel review, area means things like Convergence, Config, or Diminishing Returns; `flaw_class` is issue type. So the stop detector is monitoring the wrong partition. This is an upstream input/ownership error that can make sub-area saturation look solved when it is not.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Carry the actual review-area or task identifier into `Finding` or `add_round_from_findings()`, and drive per-area vocabulary from that real area label instead of `flaw_class`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Validation status: the claimed fixes for `4.1`, `4.2`, `4.4`, `4.5`, and `4.6` are in the code. The `4.3` decision should be reopened for the reason in `MM_F006`.
